say: When your words and your delivery disagree, people believe the delivery. Fast speech sounds nervous, so slow down for your most important sentence.

panel.heading: Make your delivery match your words
items: Pace: slow down for the key sentence
Pause two seconds after your main request
Let your voice go down at the end
Drop fillers: sorry, just, maybe
No nervous laugh after a serious sentence

say: Pause for two seconds after your main request. It gives it weight.

say: The book Difficult Conversations, from the Harvard Negotiation Project, says every hard talk is really three conversations.
The first is what happened. Each person holds only part of the story. She may not have meant to hurt you, and you were still hurt.

panel.heading: Three conversations at once

cards.d: Ask what each of us contributed, not who is to blame. Separate intention from impact.
Unspoken feelings leak out through tone and sarcasm. Name them simply.
'Am I a bad daughter-in-law if I complain?' It is about a situation, not your worth.

say: The second is feelings. If you do not name them, they leak out anyway, through tone and sarcasm.

panel.heading: Three conversations at once

say: The third is identity: what this seems to say about you. Noticing it calms you. The conversation is about a situation, not your whole worth.

say: The first sentence often decides the next ten minutes. Avoid starting with your conclusion about the other person. Treasurer, some of us are suspecting you, starts a fight.

panel.heading: Open without starting a fight

say: Instead, describe it the way an outsider would, then invite her in. The account balance and our records don't match by 12,000 naira. Can we go through it together?
And choose a private moment, not when either of you is hungry, rushed, or in front of people.

panel.heading: Open without starting a fight

say: Sometimes the hard conversation is your apology. Name what you did. I'm sorry I shared your news in the group before you were ready.

panel.heading: A sincere apology, and limits
items: Name what you did
Take responsibility, with no 'but'
Acknowledge the effect on her
Repair, and commit to change

say: Take responsibility without but. Avoid, I'm sorry if you were offended, which puts the problem back on her.

say: Acknowledge the effect. That was your story to tell, and I embarrassed you.

say: Repair and commit. I've deleted the message, and I won't share your private matters again.

say: Speaking up is never a licence to gossip, shame people publicly, threaten, or record private conversations to use against someone. Keep other people's health, money and family matters private.

say: The Center for Creative Leadership teaches feedback called Situation, Behaviour, Impact. First the situation. At yesterday's delivery.

panel.heading: Give with SBI, receive with grace
items: Situation: when and where
Behaviour: what you saw or heard
Impact: the effect, then ask a question
Receiving: listen, thank, clarify, decide

say: Then the behaviour. The three cartons arrived at 2pm instead of 10am.

panel.heading: Give with SBI, receive with grace
items: Situation: when and where
Behaviour: what you saw or heard
Impact: the effect, then ask a question
Receiving: listen, thank, clarify, decide

say: Then the impact. The customer nearly cancelled her order. What happened? It works for praise too.

say: When you receive feedback, listen to the end, thank the person, and ask, can you give me an example? Then decide calmly what is true and useful.

say: A five-minute weekly journal turns practice into evidence. Funmi counts how often she asked when she had the chance, and how much owed money came in.

say: To remember. Make your voice match your words. Prepare hard talks on all three layers, and open neutrally.
Give feedback with SBI, and receive it with thanks. And track your actions each week, so you have real proof of change.

panel.heading: Remember
items: People believe the delivery over the words
Hard talks: facts, feelings and identity
Open with a neutral description and an invitation
SBI: situation, behaviour, impact, then ask
Track your actions weekly as evidence

say: Your practice: record one real request three times, prepare one difficult conversation on a three-layer sheet, choosing one where you are safe, and start your weekly journal with SBI feedback.
